assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (proglucagon processing, incretin action, insulinotropic activity of GLP-1(7-36)) led to drugs that have transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity. Originality is high, mechanism is clear, and the clinical and societal impact is exceptional and still expanding.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and secretion of active GLP-1), Drucker (biology of GLP-1 and GLP-2 action, translational framing) and Mojsov (identification of the active peptide form) are the strongest scientific trio from the supplied names. Knudsen, a medicinal-chemistry contributor to liraglutide and semaglutide, is a credible alternative and a four-person pool exceeds the three-person limit; Mojsov's credit is contested in discussion and I cannot verify the details.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation, large outcome trials and widespread clinical use; recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation among four credited people, especially Mojsov versus Knudsen, is unresolved.
Industry-driven drug development may blur which contributions are basic discovery versus engineering.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical and other HPV-related cancers, a rare case of a vaccine directly preventing cancer. The discovery is clear and the impact is documented at population level.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (L1 VLP self-assembly and immunogenicity) and Frazer (co-development of the VLP approach and the vaccine) form a coherent trio from the credited names. Other groups worked on VLPs in parallel and priority disputes may exist, which I cannot verify.
assessment.maturity: Population-level data now show large reductions in precancer and invasive cervical cancer in vaccinated cohorts; the field is mature and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Parallel VLP work by other groups may complicate priority.
Long-term cancer-incidence data are still accumulating in some settings.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells (CAR-T) produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies, establishing a new therapeutic modality. The concept, engineering and clinical proof are all substantial.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical translation of CD19 CAR-T), Sadelain (CAR design and costimulation) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer and early gene-modified T-cell therapy) can support a fair trio, though others such as Eshhar are outside the supplied names and may be important to the credit story.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and over a decade of clinical follow-up; limited efficacy in solid tumours and toxicity remain, but the core achievement is established.
uncertainties: Credit for the original chimeric receptor concept may lie partly outside the credited names.
Solid-tumour efficacy and safety are unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense correction of SMN2 splicing yielded nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, and a proof of concept for splice-modulating RNA drugs. The mechanism connects basic RNA splicing to a dramatic clinical effect.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing-regulatory mechanism and identification of the target sequence) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and drug development) is a natural two-person configuration; Adrian Krainer's collaborators beyond the credited names may be relevant.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with several years of clinical follow-up in infants and children; durable effects and long-term outcomes continue to be characterized.
uncertainties: Relative contributions of academic and industry teams are not fully resolved by the supplied text.
Long-term outcomes across SMA types remain under study.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defines how the endoplasmic reticulum signals to the nucleus, linking proteostasis to physiology and diseases including diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer. The discovery is conceptually original and foundational.
assessment.attribution: Walter (IRE1 and Hac1/XBP1 pathway and UPR logic) and Mori (UPR element identification and signaling) are the decisive figures in the credited list and form a clean pair.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and widely confirmed in many systems; the medical translation is still developing, which tempers the direct clinical case.
uncertainties: Disease-relevant therapeutic impact is still emerging.
Recent Nobel recognition of related cell-biology topics could affect timing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics enabled causal, cell-type-specific control of neural activity and transformed experimental neuroscience, with first clinical applications emerging. The impact on research methods is very large.
assessment.attribution: Credit is broad. From the supplied names, Hegemann (channelrhodopsin characterization), Deisseroth (neuronal and in vivo implementation) and Miesenböck (early genetically targeted photostimulation) is one plausible trio, but Boyden, Bamberg and Nagel are also decisive and the three-person limit forces exclusion of significant contributors.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted for over a decade, but clinical translation is early.
uncertainties: The credit pool of six exceeds three laureates and is difficult to resolve fairly.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of cell-free fetal DNA in maternal plasma led to noninvasive prenatal testing, now routine worldwide and extended to oncology liquid biopsy. The discovery is clear, original and has major clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Credit rests clearly on Lo as the supplied single name; I cannot verify whether other groups had meaningful independent contributions.
assessment.maturity: Clinically deployed for more than a decade with extensive validation; recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Screening versus diagnostic performance limits and ethical debates remain.
Relative scope as a diagnostic technology versus a mechanistic discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR identification and the TORC1/TORC2 nutrient-sensing network is a central discovery in growth control, with relevance to cancer, metabolism, ageing and immunosuppression. The concept is deep and broadly influential.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR in yeast and defined its role in cell growth; Schreiber's work on rapamycin binding and Sabatini's mammalian mTOR work are important, but I would propose Hall alone as the clearest, with the pool of three allowing alternatives. Sabatini's circumstances are a further consideration I cannot assess here.
assessment.maturity: Highly confirmed across organisms with extensive follow-up; clinical translation through rapalogs is real but moderate.
uncertainties: Whether Hall alone or a combined configuration best reflects credit.
Therapeutic impact is narrower than the biological significance.
